previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a male with a history of primary central nervous system lymphoma in remission and prior systemic lymphoma, was admitted for evaluation of dizziness and a fall two weeks prior. Initial CT head revealed new hypodensities in the left thalamus and cerebral peduncle, prompting an MRI which showed enhancing lesions concerning for possible lymphoma recurrence or treatment-related changes such as methotrexate toxicity. A spinal tap was performed with borderline elevated protein and elevated CSF b2-microglobulin, though cytology and flow remain pending. Cultures showed no growth. A full-body CT found no evidence of systemic lymphoma. He was managed supportively with a magnesium citrate dose for constipation and monitored for falls. He remained neurologically stable with no further episodes. Discharge was planned with follow-up to determine next steps, including possible PET scan or empiric treatment. He was discharged home in stable condition on his baseline medications.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with history of CNS lymphoma (also h/o mixed hodgkins
and non-hodgkins systemic lymphoma s/p chemotherapy with 
complete
response) presents with recurrent ataxic episode. He was 
admitted recently for the same problem and found to have 
suspicious brain lesions. 

# Ataxia with CNS enhancing lesions - most concerning for 
for recurrence of CNS lymphoma other differential could include
MTX leukoencephalopathy but timing does not fit (last MTX in
___). Also less likely PML as pt not on immunosuppression,
demyelinating dz also possible. He had workup for systemic 
lymphoma in the past few weeks including PET/CT, LDH/uric acid 
wnl, SPEP w/o monoclonal protein,
b2microglobulin serum wnl, LP done ___ with no malignant cells. 


He had a repeat brain MRI while here, which shows some increase 
in his brain lesions concerning for recurrent CNS lymphoma. The 
patient was co-managed with Dr. ___ neuro-oncology. We 
decided to start an induction course of high dose methotrexate 
at 8g/m2. This was given per the usual protocol on ___ after 
urinary alkalinization. Leucovorin rescue commenced 24 hours 
later and his methotrexate level decreased as expected. 
Transaminases peaked and began to decline as expected. He did 
have significant hypokalemia, likely related to aggressive fluid 
hydration, and required PO and IV repletion. He had not 
complications from this. His symptoms of ataxia continued after 
starting methotrexate, so on ___ we started decadron 4mg 
BID. This resulted in improvement in symptoms, but after further 
discussion with patient and Dr. ___ decided to discontinue 
steroids at discharge. He will return next week for Rituxan and 
in 2 weeks for next treatment. He will have a port placed on his 
next admission. 

A total of 45 minutes was spent in discharge planning
